bull_bear.body:
- Competitive advantage in suppositories and pessaries acting as a specialised entry barrier / operational moat against standard formulation manufacturers
- Established African distribution network ensuring seamless front-end marketing and product availability
- Dedicated Kenya local presence with localized business models and direct marketing infrastructure
- Long-standing customer relationships with major global healthcare distributors and institutional buyers
- Differentiated dosage-form capabilities creating higher barriers to entry and sustained market relevance
- Capital structure reflecting net-zero debt alongside continuous working capital optimisation
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Concentration in a single material subsidiary — As on March 31, 2026, the Company's only material subsidiary under Reg. 16(1)(c) of SEBI Listing Regulations is Asterisk Lifesciences (GH) Ltd., concentrating consolidated materiality in one overseas (Ghana) entity.
- Cyber security and information risk — The Board's Risk Management Committee charter explicitly scopes information and cyber security risk within its risk-identification framework, reflecting the Company's reliance on digital systems across its operations.
- Sectoral and sustainability (ESG) risk — The Risk Management Committee's policy framework separately designates sectoral risk and sustainability/ESG-related risk as categories requiring board-level identification and monitoring.
- Financial and operational risk — Financial and operational risk are named as core categories under the Company's formal Risk Management Committee policy, framed under Regulation 21 of the SEBI Listing Regulations.
- Management transition — During FY26 the Managing Director (Mr. Gagan Harsh Sharma) and two Whole-Time Directors (Dr. Vibha Gagan Sharma and Mrs. Shruti Vishal Rao) resigned from the Board, with a new MD & CEO (Mr. S. N. Kamath) and two new Independent Directors appointed within the year, indicating an unusually high degree of leadership churn.

business.body: Bliss GVS Pharma Limited, established in 1984 and headquartered in Mumbai, manufactures, markets, trades and exports pharmaceutical formulations - including suppositories, pessaries, capsules, tablets and syrups - for international markets. It is recognised as one of the world's leading manufacturers of suppositories and pessaries, with a particularly robust footprint in Sub-Saharan Africa, which the Company states accounts for more than 80% of its sales volume.

outlook.body:
- Continue to expand geographical footprint across regulated and emerging markets
- Diversify product portfolio through innovation while enhancing operational efficiency
- Maintain robust regulatory compliance across manufacturing facilities to support growth in regulated markets
- Digital transformation of business processes and HR systems (Project JEET 2.0 - SAP S/4HANA; Project HRManch - SAP SuccessFactors)
- Disciplined capital allocation, execution excellence and customer engagement
- Reinforce risk management framework, internal controls and compliance culture
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company continued to scale its manufacturing capabilities during FY26, with significant progress at the semi-solid manufacturing facility at Vevoor, Palghar (a state-of-the-art semi-solid plant was commissioned there) alongside the expansion of suppositories and pessaries manufacturing at Unit 2, Palghar - investments the Company describes as approximately Rs 69 crores in aggregate. The Company is also executing targeted capacity expansion on suppository lines across its advanced manufacturing facilities to meet escalating global demand. Its multi-year journey includes acquisition of 28 acres of land in Vadodara, Gujarat for future expansion; commissioning of 4.5 MW and 3 MW solar power plants (at Ahmednagar and elsewhere) to reduce dependence on conventional energy; US FDA approval for the suppository manufacturing unit at Palghar; EU-GMP approvals/renewal for two manufacturing plants and Unit 2; a UK subsidiary established to drive European expansion; a branch office opened in the Philippines; commissioning of a 3rd manufacturing plant for oral solids and dry powder formulations; a herbal manufacturing facility for lozenges and a soap manufacturing facility set up in Nigeria; acquisition of a semi-solid manufacturing unit to strengthen the dermatology footprint; new facilities for Dry Powder for Injection and Ampoules; and the acquisition of a 70% stake in Kremoint Pharma, adding cream and ointment manufacturing capacity at Ambernath, Maharashtra.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global pharmaceutical industry exhibiting strong and sustained momentum, driven by increasing healthcare demand, rising prevalence of chronic diseases and improving access to treatment across emerging economies
- India's position as a cost-efficient, quality pharmaceutical hub supported by an expanding network of trade agreements enhancing global market access
- Regulated markets (US, Canada, Europe) continuing to contribute meaningfully to revenue, reflecting a compliance-focused strategy and growing portfolio of approved products
- Commencement of own operations in Kenya deepening presence in Sub-Saharan Africa, enhancing distribution efficiency and access to essential medicines
- FY2025-26 described as a year of measured progress amid challenges from evolving regulatory expectations, currency fluctuations and changing procurement patterns across geographies
- Differentiated dosage-form capabilities continuing to serve as a competitive advantage, creating higher barriers to entry and sustained market relevance
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: One of the world's leading manufacturers of suppositories and pessaries, with over four decades of specialised dosage-form expertise and a Sub-Saharan Africa-anchored global franchise across 60+ countries.

open.item: The Company is executing targeted capacity expansion on suppository lines across its advanced manufacturing facilities to support escalating global demand.

Continued scale-up of manufacturing capabilities including the semi-solid manufacturing facility at Vevoor, Palghar and expansion of suppositories and pessaries manufacturing at Unit 2, with investments amounting to approximately Rs 69 crores.
Strategic efforts continue to strengthen the Africa business by widening the therapeutic portfolio and enhancing market penetration across Sub-Saharan healthcare systems.
The Company is actively driving the increase of sales in regulated markets by expanding its product filings and commercial strategies in complex international healthcare systems.

Formally initiated digital transformation with Project JEET 2.0 (SAP S/4HANA implementation) to streamline business processes and enhance data-driven decision-making, and Project HRManch (SAP SuccessFactors) for talent management, employee development and workforce planning.
